To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a web application that uses Watson Web Services for the analysis of German court decisions, which can be used for the evaluation of the BGH decisions.

we were able to: - Automatically classify the outcome of over 50,00 court decisions - Automatically extract entities from the court decisions - Create an interface that allows users to explore statistics on judges, courts, senates and more - Provide explanations of the classification decisions based on relevant sentences in the court decision - Provide links to the original court decision in the German Federal Court of Justice database (https://www.bundesgerichtshof.de/)

we were able to build a system that can automatically classify the outcome of court decisions with an accuracy of 80.2% and can extract the names of the judges, senates and previous instances with 95% accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can we automatically classify court decisions from the BGH based on their outcome?
the question of whether ML-based NLP can be used for the analysis of court decisions.
the following aspects: • How can we use NLP and ML for the analysis of court decisions in the legal domain?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tool can provide a valuable service for legal practitioners and scholars alike.
the application is a valuable tool for legal professionals, researchers and the general public alike.
the application of Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing to the analysis of German court decisions is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now use ML and NLP for a first step in the direction of a “Google for Court Decisions” in the German legal domain.
we have developed a tool that provides quantitative insights into the German court decision corpus, which can be used by law professionals.
we have developed a scalable and modular architecture for a large scale NLP application that provides a foundation for further research in this domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ML can be used to extract and analyze large quantities of legal data.
it is possible to build a tool that can automatically extract information from large amounts of legal text and provide it as a service.
ML-based NLP techniques can provide a valuable tool for legal scholars, researchers, and law professionals to gain insights from large-scale court data.
